content.prompt: Find the range of each function.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=(\sin^2x+\cos^2x)^2-2\sin^2x\cos^2x\\&=1-\frac12(2\sin x\cos x)^2\\&=1-\frac12\sin^22x.\end{aligned}$$
Since $0\leq\sin^22x\leq1$,
$$\begin{aligned}1-\frac12\leq y\leq1\end{aligned}$$
so the range is $\dfrac12\leq y\leq1$.

$$\begin{aligned}y&=(\sin^2x+\cos^2x)(\sin^4x-\sin^2x\cos^2x+\cos^4x)\\&=(\sin^4x+\cos^4x)-\sin^2x\cos^2x\\&=1-3\sin^2x\cos^2x\\&=1-\frac34(2\sin x\cos x)^2\\&=1-\frac34\sin^22x.\end{aligned}$$
Since $0\leq\sin^22x\leq1$,
$$1-\frac34\leq y\leq1$$
so the range is $\dfrac14\leq y\leq1$.

classification.difficultyReason: There is no signposting. Students must rewrite sin⁴+cos⁴ and sin⁶+cos⁶ as 1−2s²c² and 1−3s²c² (including the sum of cubes), convert to sin²2x, and then bound it to find the range. This needs non-trivial algebraic reframing.

sourceAtom.label: Example
sourceAtom.visibleSubtitle: Integrate odd powers of sin x and cos x

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\sin^3 x&=\sin x(1-\cos^2 x)\end{align*}$$
Let $u=\cos x$, so $du=-\sin x\,dx$.

The limits become $u=1$ when $x=0$, and $u=0$ when $x=\frac\pi2$.
$$\begin{align*}\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^3 x\,dx&=-\int_1^0(1-u^2)\,du\\&=\int_0^1(1-u^2)\,du\\&=\left[u-\frac{u^3}{3}\right]_0^1\\&=\frac23\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\cos^3 x&=\cos x(1-\sin^2 x)\end{align*}$$
Let $u=\sin x$, so $du=\cos x\,dx$.
$$\begin{align*}\int\cos^3 x\,dx&=\int(1-u^2)\,du\\&=u-\frac{u^3}{3}+C\\&=\sin x-\frac{\sin^3 x}{3}+C\end{align*}$$
